title: Hospital fragmentation and second readmission after heart failure
text:
Among adults hospitalized for heart failure whose index and first-readmission discharges are recorded as alive, and whose first readmission occurs within 30 days, is discharge from the same hospital rather than a different hospital associated with another readmission within 30 days?
The study uses US Nationwide Readmissions Database records from 2016-2022. The analysis accounts for the database’s hospital sampling design and uses discharge weights. The results describe an association among people who reached the second stage of this care pathway. They do not estimate what would happen if a hospital changed its referral or transfer practices.

The study uses US Nationwide Readmissions Database records from 2016-2022. The analysis accounts for the database’s hospital sampling design and uses discharge weights. The results describe an association among people who reached the second stage of this care pathway. They do not estimate what would happen if a hospital changed its referral or transfer practices.

title: Hospital fragmentation and second readmission after heart failure
text:
Main findings
The adjusted model estimates a 30-day second-readmission risk of 31.4% (31.3% to 31.6%) for patients whose first readmission was at the same hospital, and 32.5% (32.2% to 32.8%) for those readmitted to a different hospital. The adjusted risk difference (different minus same hospital) was 1.1 percentage points (95% CI 0.7 to 1.4 percentage points). The adjusted risk ratio was 1.034 (95% CI 1.023 to 1.045).
These adjusted values come from the primary model, which includes measured patient and hospital characteristics available in the database. A separate conditional model adds measured characteristics of the first readmission. Both estimates may still reflect differences the data could not measure.

text:
How the cohort was formed
The yearly counts below show eligible first heart failure discharges, first readmissions within 30 days before the known-alive eligibility screen, and the second-stage population recorded as alive at first-readmission discharge (DIED=0). Deaths and records with unknown death status are excluded before this second-stage population is formed. Weighted counts are national estimates. The seven years are analyzed with year-specific linkage and survey identifiers; patient links do not cross calendar years.

Unmeasured confounding
The E-value is calculated from the directly standardized adjusted risk ratio and its lower confidence limit. It does not show that such confounding is present or absent.

title: Hospital fragmentation and second readmission after heart failure
text:
Methods in brief
The analytic population begins with adults whose principal heart failure hospitalization is recorded as discharged alive from January through October. It then requires a first 30-day readmission recorded as alive at discharge (DIED=0) by November, leaving the full 30-day window observable within that calendar year. The first-readmission flow count precedes the known-alive screen; patients with an in-hospital death or unknown death status are not eligible for the second-stage risk set. Transfers are excluded from the readmission risk set because the hospital attribution or follow-up for the next event is not defined consistently for those discharges. The exposure compares whether that first readmission was to the same hospital as the index stay or to a different hospital. The outcome is any further inpatient readmission within 30 days after the first readmission.
The models account for the NRD’s stratified hospital sampling design and discharge weights. The primary model adjusts for calendar year and measured patient and hospital characteristics. A separate conditional model also adjusts for measured first-readmission characteristics. The analysis uses annual linkage identifiers because NRD patient linkage is limited to each calendar year. See the analysis code and aggregate tables for the full variable definitions and model specification.

title: Hospital fragmentation and second readmission after heart failure
text:
Limitations
This is an observational analysis of administrative discharge records. The primary complete-case model includes 502,236 discharges from 512,770 eligible second-stage discharges; records missing required model covariates are excluded. Differences between patients treated at the same or different hospitals may reflect clinical severity, access to care, referral patterns, or social factors unavailable in the database, leaving residual confounding. Diagnosis codes do not provide the clinical detail of a medical record, and coding may be incomplete. Readmissions outside the NRD’s observable linkage are not captured, including care across state boundaries and events after the annual linkage window. Out-of-hospital deaths are not observed, so some patients classified as at risk may have died before a recorded readmission. Patients who die during a hospitalization cannot experience a subsequent readmission and are outside this conditional prognosis estimand. The results are adjusted associations among survivors who experienced a first readmission, not causal effects of hospital continuity or fragmentation.

Reproducibility and data access
The analysis uses the HCUP Nationwide Readmissions Database, which requires an authorized data-use agreement. The analysis source code and the aggregate tables used to produce this report are available in the project repository. The aggregate tables can also be downloaded individually below. They contain summary results only; record-level data and survey sampling files are not included.
